title: Eating Zoom
description: An eating zoom is a crash into the bite, chopsticks or spoon as the last foreground, appetite as a punch-in. The move is optical and short; the dish should be nameable in the last frame.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The bite is the cut. Noodles, a first date, a villain who eats too well: the camera snaps to food meeting mouth.
Comic or sensual depends on how kind the light is. A wide dinner master does not want this.
If you still see the restaurant, you did not crash. If there is no food in the last frame, you shot a mouth-in.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Write a snap zoom, under a second, ending on the bite. Hold.
Do not dolly. Show steam, gloss, or dripping as proof of the food.
The face can be partial. Prompt: Eating zoom on [Subject], a crash into the bite, chopsticks or spoon as the last foreground, appetite as a punch-in.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a mouth-in or a restaurant wide. The tell: no food in the last frame, or the whole dining room still visible.
The fix: snap into the bite, utensil as last foreground, hold.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Eating Zoom in film?
An eating zoom is a crash zoom into a bite, with food or a utensil as the last foreground. Appetite is the punch-in.
Eating Zoom vs Mouth In
Mouth in enters the mouth as landscape. Eating zoom is optical and food-first: the crash ends on the bite.
When should I use Eating Zoom?
Use it when the bite is the event. Do not use it as coverage of a whole dinner table.
How do I prompt Eating Zoom for AI image or video?
Write a snap into food meeting mouth. Example: Eating zoom on [Subject], a crash into the bite, chopsticks or spoon as the last foreground.
